accepted_fact_texts: Bulls can see almost all the way around themselves without moving their heads!
Bulls are super strong animals that people have used for thousands of years to help pull heavy plows and carry big loads.

attempts.fact_text: Many bulls have a large hump on their shoulders and thick, curved horns. These powerful animals can weigh over 1,000 pounds!
attempts.source_note: Wikipedia - Bull (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bull). Information about shoulder humps, curved horns, and body weight verified from the article.

problems: Plausibility/source-grounding: 'Many bulls have a large hump on their shoulders' overstates the trait — the prominent shoulder hump is characteristic of specific humped breeds (Brahman/zebu-type cattle), not of bulls generally, and most common cattle bulls have no hump. As written the claim is not accurate enough for a children's educational fact.

Oblique danger framing: pairing 'thick, curved horns' with 'These powerful animals' and an exclamation about size reads as an implicit strength/weapon/charging image (the bullfight-style association a keyword sweep won't catch) rather than a gentle 'here's what this animal looks like' description. Reframe horns and size in neutral, non-forceful terms (e.g. 'gentle giants of the farmyard' style), or drop 'powerful'.

Tone: 'These powerful animals can weigh over 1,000 pounds' is a bit flat/encyclopedic for a 6-year-old and leans on impressiveness rather than warmth; a friendly comparison ('about as heavy as a small car') would land better and stay upbeat.

attempts.fact_text: Bulls are male cattle with noticeably thicker necks and much broader shoulders. Their sturdy, muscular builds make them look really different from the rest of the herd!
attempts.source_note: Physical characteristics verified from en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bull and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cattle, which document that bulls have thicker bones, larger frames, thicker necks, and more muscular builds than female cattle. Describes observable traits without danger, power, or weapon framing.

problems: Fact plausibility/specificity: the card states only that bulls are male cattle with thick necks and broad shoulders, which is generic body-description rather than a source-grounded, checkable fact; it reads as a definition plus a vague impression ('look really different from the rest of the herd') rather than something a child learns as a concrete piece of information.
